items.prompt:
An advantageous heritable trait tends to ____ in proportion over generations.
A) increase
B) decrease
C) stay the same forever
D) disappear instantly

We track a trait's change by measuring
A) the percentage with the trait each generation
B) the weather
C) the time
D) the color of the lab
items.answer: A) the percentage with the trait each generation

steps: Measuring the proportion tracks the change.

items.prompt:
Dark moths rising from 20 to 70 percent in a sooty forest supports that
A) the advantageous trait is spreading by natural selection
B) nothing is happening
C) moths choose their color
D) the forest is shrinking
items.answer: A) the advantageous trait is spreading by natural selection

items.prompt:
An advantageous trait increases because its carriers
A) reproduce more and pass it on
B) reproduce less
C) never reproduce
D) change the weather
items.answer: A) reproduce more and pass it on

items.prompt:
A trait stays at 10 percent each generation. This suggests it is
A) not giving a selective advantage
B) strongly advantageous
C) harmful
D) new
items.answer: A) not giving a selective advantage

steps: A steady proportion suggests no advantage.

items.prompt:
A trait goes 25 to 45 to 65 percent over three generations. The proportion is
A) rising, supporting selection
B) falling
C) unchanged
D) random

steps: A steady rise supports natural selection.

items.prompt:
Tracking a trait's proportion over generations provides
A) statistical evidence about natural selection
B) no information
C) only the trait's color
D) the weather
items.answer: A) statistical evidence about natural selection

steps: Proportion data give evidence of selection.

items.prompt:
If a harmful heritable trait is tracked over generations, its proportion would likely
A) decrease
B) increase
C) stay the same
D) double each time

steps: Harmful traits tend to decrease in proportion.
